request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Patient Name: Anonymous
Medical Record Number: N/A
Gender: Female
Age: 29 years
Date of Admission: N/A
Date of Discharge: N/A

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted to the hospital for treatment of HIV infection.

Hospital Course:
During the admission, the patient was started on ART, and 186 SMS text messages were sent and received to remind her to take medication. The patient responded to only 28% of the text messages and did not respond to the remaining 72%. During feedback sessions, the patient claimed to have taken medication as per the instructions given and responded to all the text messages. Later, during an interview, the patient disclosed that she was not honest during the feedback sessions as she was depressed about unwanted disclosure of her HIV status and stigma related to HIV. She also mentioned that she deletes the SMS text messages once she replies to them to avoid any possible disclosure of her status.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Condition:
The patient will be discharged once her treatment is completed.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is instructed to continue with ART medication as per the instructions given by the healthcare provider. The patient is also advised to follow up with the healthcare provider as per the scheduled appointments and to disclose any concerns or issues related to her treatment. The patient is also requested to maintain the confidentiality of her HIV status and not to reveal it to anyone without proper authorization. 

Signatures:
The discharge summary was dictated by the healthcare provider and reviewed and approved by the medical transcriptionist.

Dictated by: Dr. Sample
Reviewed by: John Doe, MT

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: B24**

The episode was admitted for treatment of HIV infection and the patient was started on ART, so HIV disease is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission.

- **Chapter letter, B:** HIV disease is classified with infectious and parasitic diseases.
- **Category, B24 (unspecified HIV disease):**
  - The summary names no HIV-related manifestation, such as an opportunistic infection or malignancy, so B20–B23 do not apply.
  - The patient was admitted for active treatment of HIV infection, so Z21 (asymptomatic HIV status) is not appropriate.
- **Depression and stigma:** these affected her adherence and could be coded as additional diagnoses. They were not the reason for the admission, so they are not the principal diagnosis.
